phases.name: Frame the serverless workload and trust boundaries
phases.description: Separate prompt facts from assumptions, establish identity and payment boundaries, then build the public request and media paths.

phases.name: Serve the catalog and protect the transactional order path
phases.description: Use managed compute and fit-for-purpose data paths; keep cached catalog reads separate from strongly consistent inventory reservations.

phases.name: Make order processing durable and payment-safe
phases.description: Bridge the atomic order transaction to asynchronous orchestration with an outbox, then model payment as an idempotent saga with recoverable notifications.

phases.name: Publish inventory changes and prove scale behavior
phases.description: Fan out committed inventory changes to live clients, expose operational signals, and validate burst, concurrency, cost, latency, and recovery assumptions.

steps.phase: Frame the serverless workload and trust boundaries
steps.title: Distinguish stated requirements from sizing assumptions
steps.content: The brief asks for catalog management, orders and payments, authenticated sessions, product media, sales-spike handling, live inventory updates, order confirmations, and automatic scaling. Its explicit constraints are cost-effective variable traffic, cold starts under one second, 10,000+ concurrent users, secure payment transactions, and ACID order properties. It does not specify peak requests per second, read/write mix, availability target, live-update freshness, region policy, or order volume. Treat those as discovery questions; size concurrency from measured request rate × duration rather than equating 10,000 signed-in users with 10,000 simultaneous Lambda executions.

steps.phase: Frame the serverless workload and trust boundaries
steps.title: Plan for active sessions and burst rates, not a single average
steps.content: Use 10,000+ concurrent users as a required load-test population, but first measure the fraction active at once, API requests per active user, and handler duration. Replay a sharp sale-start burst and a sustained sale plateau. Check API Gateway quotas, Lambda regional and per-function concurrency, DynamoDB partition distribution, WebSocket connection quotas, SQS age, and downstream payment-provider limits before launch; request quota increases early where measured headroom is insufficient.

decision.question: What does the 10,000+ concurrent-user constraint mean for capacity planning?
decision.chosen: Load-test at least 10,000 active user sessions and derive in-flight requests and service quotas from observed request rate and latency; do not assume one Lambda invocation per logged-in user.
decision.chosenReason: Concurrency is a workload property. This makes the constraint testable without inventing an unstated requests-per-second target.

alternatives.tradeoff: Can waste money during quiet periods and still miss burst, duration, or downstream quota bottlenecks.

alternatives.option: Treat the user count as equivalent to requests per second
alternatives.tradeoff: Confuses connected users with request arrival rate and produces unreliable sizing.

steps.phase: Frame the serverless workload and trust boundaries
steps.title: Keep raw card data outside the application boundary
steps.content: Use a PCI-compliant payment provider's hosted fields or tokenization flow. The platform should persist only provider tokens, payment intent/reference IDs, outcome, amount, and audit metadata; never log or store PAN or CVV. The provider call is an external side effect, so it cannot join a DynamoDB ACID transaction; make it a saga step with a stable idempotency key, verified callbacks, bounded retries, and compensation.

decision.question: How should order ACID guarantees coexist with an external card processor?
decision.chosen: Atomically create the order, reserve inventory, and write an outbox event in DynamoDB; then orchestrate tokenized payment as an idempotent Step Functions saga with explicit success, retry, timeout, and compensation paths.
decision.chosenReason: The local order invariant remains transactional while the external payment side effect is handled with durable, replay-safe workflow state.

alternatives.option: Call the processor inside a database transaction
alternatives.tradeoff: A remote network call cannot be made atomic with DynamoDB and can hold locks or reservations across unpredictable latency.

alternatives.option: Retry every payment timeout as a new charge
alternatives.tradeoff: An ambiguous response can create duplicate charges.

steps.phase: Frame the serverless workload and trust boundaries
steps.title: Represent shoppers and authenticated sellers
steps.content: This client boundary includes browser and mobile shoppers plus seller/admin users. Give catalog write operations a seller role while shoppers receive only the catalog, cart, order, and subscription permissions they need. The client sends a stable checkout idempotency key and does not treat a successful button click as proof of payment.

component.label: Shopper + Seller Clients
component.description: Browser/mobile storefront and authenticated catalog console

properties.purpose: Browse catalog and media, authenticate, submit idempotent checkout requests, and subscribe to live inventory; seller/admin catalog writes require a separate authorized role.

component.highlightReason: The existing Web App palette component represents the human and seller client boundary without inventing a node type.

steps.phase: Frame the serverless workload and trust boundaries
steps.title: Add an edge security and bot-control boundary
steps.content: Use AWS WAF managed rules and carefully tuned bot/rate controls in front of the REST and WebSocket API stages. Apply per-identity/API throttles and validation at the API boundary as well; WAF mitigates abusive traffic but is not a replacement for application authorization or payment idempotency.

component.label: AWS WAF
component.description: Managed rules and abuse controls at API edges

properties.purpose: Protect REST and WebSocket API stages with managed rules, request-size limits, and tuned bot/rate controls; alert on blocks and avoid rules that reject legitimate sale traffic.
properties.rules: Managed baseline plus reviewed application-specific rules; no payment secrets or card data in logs

component.highlightReason: The catalog Firewall component is the existing representation for WAF and edge filtering.

steps.phase: Frame the serverless workload and trust boundaries
steps.title: Create the REST API boundary
steps.content: Expose versioned catalog, seller, cart, checkout, order-status, and inventory-read endpoints through API Gateway. Validate payload sizes and schemas, authenticate protected routes, enforce per-client throttles, and return an order-pending response only after the transaction and outbox event are durable.

component.label: Storefront REST API
component.description: Validated, authenticated, throttled HTTPS endpoints

properties.purpose: Route versioned catalog, seller, checkout, order-status, and inventory-read endpoints; validate schemas and payload limits; require JWT/role checks on protected routes; acknowledge checkout only after durable order/outbox commit.
properties.inputValidation: Strict schemas, size limits, price/quantity validation, and server-side price lookup
properties.authentication: JWT authorizer; role-based seller/admin checks; anonymous access only to explicitly public catalog reads
properties.rateLimiting: Per-client and per-route throttles with stricter checkout and login abuse controls
properties.deduplication: Require stable checkout idempotency key and persist its outcome with the order

component.highlightReason: API Gateway is the catalog's existing component for HTTPS request routing and API-level protections.

steps.phase: Frame the serverless workload and trust boundaries
steps.title: Route shopper traffic through edge protection
steps.content: Send shopper and seller requests through the same edge control, then let API Gateway apply route-specific authentication and throttling. The WAF decision is not authorization: seller permissions are checked against the authenticated identity in the application path.

connection.label: HTTPS storefront + seller traffic
connection.description: WAF evaluates requests before protected API routes

steps.phase: Frame the serverless workload and trust boundaries
steps.title: Forward inspected requests to API Gateway
steps.content: Only the protected API stage is reachable from this edge path. Apply distinct route quotas so a catalog sale burst cannot consume all checkout or authentication capacity, and return retry guidance rather than silently dropping throttled requests.

connection.label: Inspected HTTPS requests
connection.description: WAF-protected REST routes with API quotas and schema validation

steps.phase: Frame the serverless workload and trust boundaries
steps.title: Add the managed identity and session service
steps.content: Use a managed identity provider such as Amazon Cognito for signup/login, JWT issuance, refresh-token rotation, and MFA for seller/admin accounts. Keep authorization decisions scoped to user and tenant roles, and never trust a client-supplied price, role, or inventory count.

component.label: Identity + Session Provider
component.description: Managed sign-in, JWTs, refresh, and seller MFA

properties.purpose: Use a managed IdP (for example Cognito) for authentication, JWT issuance, refresh-token rotation, account recovery, and seller/admin MFA; enforce user and seller roles server-side.
properties.oauth: OAuth 2.0 / OIDC authorization-code flow with PKCE for public clients
properties.sessions: Short-lived access tokens, rotated refresh tokens, revocation and logout
properties.tokenTTL: Short-lived access token; choose exact TTL from risk and UX policy

component.highlightReason: Auth Service is an existing palette component for identity and session lifecycle.

steps.phase: Frame the serverless workload and trust boundaries
steps.title: Authorize protected routes with verified identity claims
steps.content: The API authorizer validates issuer, audience, signature, expiry, and required scopes/roles. Catalog writes require a seller/admin claim; checkout derives customer identity from the token, not the request body. Keep public product reads explicitly separate from privileged routes.

connection.label: OIDC/JWT authorization
connection.description: API validates token claims and route roles; identity service owns login and session lifecycle

steps.phase: Frame the serverless workload and trust boundaries
steps.title: Add the product-media delivery edge
steps.content: Serve immutable, versioned product images from CloudFront so repeated catalog reads do not invoke application Lambdas or repeatedly fetch the origin. Use short-lived signed upload URLs for authorized sellers and a reviewed cache-invalidation/versioning policy for changed media.

component.label: CloudFront Product Media CDN
component.description: Cache static product images near shoppers

properties.purpose: Deliver versioned public product media from S3; use immutable object keys, safe cache headers, origin access control, and targeted invalidation only when an object must change in place.
properties.ttl: Long TTL for versioned media; honor explicit cache policy
properties.cacheInvalidation: Prefer versioned keys; invalidate only on exceptional replacement

component.highlightReason: The existing CDN component accurately represents CloudFront's media edge.

steps.phase: Frame the serverless workload and trust boundaries
steps.title: Store product images and media in object storage
steps.content: Store original and derived product media in S3 with versioning, encryption, checksums, lifecycle policy, and tightly scoped seller upload permissions. Keep the bucket private; CloudFront uses origin access control, and uploads use constrained presigned URLs rather than public write access.

component.label: Private Product Media Bucket (S3)
component.description: Versioned, encrypted image and media origin

properties.purpose: Private origin for product images and media; enforce encryption, origin access control, seller-scoped presigned writes, checksum validation, versioning, and lifecycle retention.

component.highlightReason: Object Storage is the existing palette component for S3; it supports the media-origin role without a custom node.

steps.phase: Frame the serverless workload and trust boundaries
steps.title: Connect the CDN to the private media origin
steps.content: CloudFront fetches media from S3 through origin access control; browsers never receive bucket write credentials. Validate content type/size during seller upload and serve only approved object paths.

connection.label: OAC origin fetch
connection.description: CloudFront reads private versioned media from S3

steps.phase: Frame the serverless workload and trust boundaries
steps.title: Serve media independently of the API path
steps.content: Clients request static images from the CDN rather than proxying every byte through API Gateway and Lambda. This lowers origin work and keeps sale traffic from turning media downloads into compute invocations.

connection.label: Cached product media
connection.description: Shopper clients fetch images directly from CloudFront

steps.phase: Frame the serverless workload and trust boundaries
steps.title: Keep cardholder data out of logs and storage
steps.content: Redact authorization headers, tokens, payment references where needed, and all payment secrets from application logs and traces. Encrypt data in transit and at rest, scope IAM roles per function, and audit seller catalog writes and payment-state transitions. WAF and authentication do not replace PCI scope review with the payment provider.

steps.phase: Frame the serverless workload and trust boundaries
steps.title: Use the same edge boundary for live API sessions
steps.content: The live-inventory WebSocket endpoint will use its own API Gateway stage but remains behind the same WAF policy. Authenticate the WebSocket connect route, bind subscriptions to the verified user/tenant, and expire stale connection records; a guessed connection ID must never grant access to another customer's inventory scope.

steps.phase: Serve the catalog and protect the transactional order path
steps.title: Add the catalog Lambda
steps.content: Keep catalog reads and seller catalog mutations in a focused Lambda handler with separate authorization and validation branches. Look up price and product status server-side at checkout; a browser's displayed price is not authoritative.

component.label: Catalog + Seller Lambda
component.description: Product reads, validated seller writes, and media URL issuance

properties.purpose: Serve product reads and authorized seller create/update operations; validate ownership and fields, issue constrained presigned media URLs, and emit cache invalidation/version changes after committed updates.
properties.runtime: Small supported runtime selected from team skills and cold-start benchmarks
properties.timeout: Short bounded request handler; tune from traces
properties.concurrency: Reserved capacity for catalog isolation with target-tracked provisioned concurrency only where measured latency requires it
properties.coldStart: Keep package and initialization lean; provision warm concurrency for latency-critical peaks and verify cold-start distribution under load

component.highlightReason: Serverless Function is the existing palette component for Lambda business logic.

steps.phase: Serve the catalog and protect the transactional order path
steps.title: Store catalog records in DynamoDB
steps.content: Choose keys and indexes from product lookup patterns: product ID, category/brand listings, seller-owned products, and deliberate sort order. Use on-demand capacity initially for uncertain variable traffic, then compare measured cost and throttling against provisioned capacity with autoscaling. Keep catalog records distinct from reservation invariants when that makes access patterns and permissions clearer.

component.label: Product Catalog (DynamoDB)
component.description: Product metadata and query-pattern indexes

properties.purpose: Store product metadata and seller ownership; define partition/sort keys and GSIs for product ID, category listings, and seller management from measured access patterns. Use on-demand capacity while traffic is uncertain, encryption, PITR, and least-privilege access.
properties.workload: Product reads and authorized seller catalog writes; variable sale traffic

component.highlightReason: The catalog Database component represents DynamoDB using editable engine and workload properties.

steps.phase: Serve the catalog and protect the transactional order path
steps.title: Cache only safe catalog responses
steps.content: Use a short, explicit TTL for popular product/category reads if measurements justify it; invalidate or version entries after seller updates. Never use this cache as the authority for inventory availability, price at checkout, order state, or payment outcome.

component.label: Hot Catalog Cache
component.description: Short-lived product-read acceleration

properties.purpose: Optionally cache popular product/category reads with a bounded TTL and explicit invalidation/versioning; never cache authoritative inventory reservations, checkout prices, payment results, or order state.
properties.engine: Managed Redis-compatible cache if load tests justify it
properties.ttl: Short measured TTL; invalidate/version on product update

component.highlightReason: Cache is an existing component for hot read acceleration, with a stated boundary around transactional data.

steps.phase: Serve the catalog and protect the transactional order path
steps.title: Route catalog requests to Lambda
steps.content: API Gateway invokes the catalog handler for public reads and authenticated seller writes. Apply role checks and price/product-state validation server-side, and keep media bytes on the CDN path.

connection.label: Catalog + seller routes
connection.description: Validated route invokes the focused catalog Lambda

steps.phase: Serve the catalog and protect the transactional order path
steps.title: Read and update catalog records
steps.content: The function accesses DynamoDB through a narrowly scoped IAM role. Seller updates should be conditional on ownership/version and should publish a cache-version change only after the write succeeds.

connection.label: Product query + seller writes
connection.description: Least-privilege DynamoDB access keyed by product and seller access patterns

steps.phase: Serve the catalog and protect the transactional order path
steps.title: Accelerate repeat product reads
steps.content: Only responses safe under the chosen freshness policy flow through the catalog cache. A catalog cache miss or outage falls back to DynamoDB within a bounded timeout; checkout re-reads authoritative price and inventory regardless of cached product-page data.

connection.label: Non-authoritative catalog cache
connection.description: Cache-aside product reads; checkout bypasses cached price and inventory

steps.phase: Serve the catalog and protect the transactional order path
steps.title: Make the cold-start target an observed SLO candidate
steps.content: The brief's under-one-second cold-start limit is a hard design constraint, but the runtime, memory, initialization work, and percentile are unspecified. Keep dependencies and initialization small; use provisioned concurrency with target tracking for measured latency-critical functions and scheduled pre-warming when sale times are known. Evaluate SnapStart only for supported runtimes. Verify cold starts separately from warm handler latency, including p95/p99 and cost; do not claim the target is met until measured.

properties.coldStart: Constraint: cold starts <1s. Keep init/package lean; provisioned concurrency with target tracking for measured latency-critical periods; benchmark cold p95/p99 and cost before claiming compliance.

steps.phase: Serve the catalog and protect the transactional order path
steps.title: Keep reservation decisions on the authoritative path
steps.content: A cached product page can be slightly stale; a successful stock reservation cannot. At checkout, recompute the price and reserve quantity using a conditional transactional write. Publish availability changes asynchronously only after the authoritative transaction commits.

steps.phase: Serve the catalog and protect the transactional order path
steps.title: Add the checkout and order Lambda
steps.content: This handler validates the authenticated customer, cart quantities, current price, and idempotency key, then conditionally reserves stock and creates a pending order. It returns a stable order ID and pending state after the local transaction commits; payment confirmation happens later in the durable workflow.

component.label: Checkout + Order Lambda
component.description: Validate cart and atomically create pending order/reservation

properties.purpose: Derive customer identity from JWT; validate cart and current catalog price; require a stable idempotency key; transact order creation, inventory reservation, and outbox write; return pending order only after commit.
properties.runtime: Small supported runtime selected from measured cold-start and team-operation needs
properties.timeout: Bounded synchronous transaction handler; no payment-provider call
properties.concurrency: Reserved capacity to isolate checkout; scale against measured peak RPS and downstream quotas
properties.coldStart: Lean initialization plus provisioned concurrency/target tracking for latency-critical sale windows; verify <1s cold-start constraint under test

component.highlightReason: A separate Lambda isolates the transactional checkout path from catalog read bursts.

steps.phase: Serve the catalog and protect the transactional order path
steps.title: Create the order and inventory transaction store
steps.content: Use an order/inventory table design whose keys make stock reservation and order lookup conditional and transactional. A DynamoDB TransactWriteItems operation can atomically create the order, decrement or reserve stock only when sufficient quantity remains, and write an outbox item in the same Region/account; stay within transaction item/size limits and model hot SKU contention explicitly.

component.label: Orders + Inventory (DynamoDB)
component.description: Transactional order state, reservations, idempotency, and outbox

properties.purpose: Persist orders, inventory reservations, checkout idempotency outcomes, and transactional outbox records; use conditional writes and TransactWriteItems for order + reservation + outbox atomicity. Keep all transaction items in a supported same-account/Region boundary and design hot-SKU contention deliberately.
properties.workload: Transactional order writes, inventory reservations, order status reads, and outbox events

component.highlightReason: The catalog Database component represents the authoritative DynamoDB transaction store.

steps.phase: Serve the catalog and protect the transactional order path
steps.title: Route checkout separately from catalog reads
steps.content: The API uses a dedicated checkout handler so catalog cache behavior and request bursts do not blur order correctness. Enforce authenticated customer ownership on every order read and mutation.

connection.label: Checkout + order routes
connection.description: Authenticated, idempotent order operations use the transactional handler

steps.phase: Serve the catalog and protect the transactional order path
steps.title: Commit reservation and pending order atomically
steps.content: The conditional transaction rejects overselling and duplicate checkout attempts. The order begins in PENDING_PAYMENT; a duplicate idempotency key returns its original order result rather than creating another reservation or payment intent.

connection.label: ACID order + stock reservation
connection.description: Conditional TransactWriteItems includes order, inventory reservation, idempotency record, and outbox

steps.phase: Serve the catalog and protect the transactional order path
steps.title: State the ACID boundary precisely
steps.content: The database transaction protects local order invariants: there is one idempotent order, stock is reserved only if enough remains, and the outbox event exists if and only if that commit succeeds. It does not make a card-network charge atomic. Use explicit PENDING_PAYMENT, CONFIRMED, FAILED, and COMPENSATING transitions with conditional version checks; reconcile ambiguous provider outcomes before retrying capture.

decision.question: Which operations must be atomic at checkout?
decision.chosen: Atomically create the pending order, reserve inventory, persist the idempotency result, and write the workflow outbox record; run payment and later state transitions as a durable idempotent saga.
decision.chosenReason: This guarantees local ACID properties without making a false distributed-transaction promise about an external processor.

alternatives.option: Decrement stock, then separately create the order
alternatives.tradeoff: A failure between writes can leak inventory or create an order without stock.

alternatives.option: Call payment first and write the order afterward
alternatives.tradeoff: A database failure after a successful charge leaves an untracked payment.

steps.phase: Serve the catalog and protect the transactional order path
steps.title: Make the database's operational assumptions explicit
steps.content: Use on-demand capacity while the traffic curve is uncertain, then compare cost with provisioned capacity and autoscaling using actual sale traces. Enable PITR and encryption, monitor throttles and hot keys, and add conditional writes/transaction idempotency rather than relying on eventual reads for stock correctness.

properties.workload: On-demand initially for variable sales; evaluate provisioned autoscaling against measured workload and cost. ACID reservation uses conditional transactions; enable PITR, encryption, alarms for throttling/hot-key contention, and same-Region recovery procedures.

steps.phase: Make order processing durable and payment-safe
steps.title: Relay committed outbox events from the database stream
steps.content: A DynamoDB Streams-triggered Lambda reads only committed outbox records and publishes them to the order queue. It checkpoints safely, tolerates replay, and marks each event by stable order/event ID; if delivery fails, retry or route to a failure path without losing the committed order.

component.label: DynamoDB Stream Outbox Relay
component.description: Replay-safe publisher for committed order events

properties.purpose: Consume committed outbox records from DynamoDB Streams and publish stable event/order IDs to SQS; handle at-least-once delivery idempotently, bound retries, expose iterator age, and preserve failed records for replay/DLQ handling.
properties.concurrency: Tune batch size and event-source concurrency to downstream queue capacity

component.highlightReason: Serverless Function is the existing Lambda component; DynamoDB Streams is an integration detail of the flow, not a new node type.

steps.phase: Make order processing durable and payment-safe
steps.title: Trigger the relay from committed database changes
steps.content: The stream carries the durable outbox boundary; consumers may see the same record again, so the relay must be idempotent. Alert on iterator age and failed batches before outbox delivery falls behind the user-visible order workflow.

connection.label: DynamoDB Streams: committed outbox
connection.description: At-least-once change stream invokes the idempotent relay after transaction commit

steps.phase: Make order processing durable and payment-safe
steps.title: Buffer order workflow starts across a sale burst
steps.content: SQS absorbs short-term workflow-start and downstream processing bursts while keeping the order transaction independent of payment-provider throughput. Configure visibility timeout above consumer duration, bounded retries, redrive to a DLQ, and alarms on oldest-message age; a queue buffers demand but does not create downstream capacity.

component.label: Durable Order Workflow Queue (SQS)
component.description: Burst buffer and replay boundary for committed orders

properties.purpose: Buffer committed order events across sale spikes; retain stable event/order IDs, configure visibility timeout above processing time, bounded retries with backoff, DLQ/redrive, and oldest-message alarms.
properties.visibilityTimeout: Greater than max consumer batch duration; tune from measured processing time
properties.backoff: Exponential backoff with jitter; redrive exhausted messages to an alarmed DLQ

component.highlightReason: Queue is the existing palette component matching SQS buffering, retries, and replay.

steps.phase: Make order processing durable and payment-safe
steps.title: Publish each outbox event to SQS
steps.content: The relay publishes an idempotent order event. A queue send retry can duplicate delivery; the workflow uses order ID plus workflow version as its execution key and checks durable order state before taking action.

connection.label: Committed order event
connection.description: Outbox relay publishes a replay-safe message to durable SQS

steps.phase: Make order processing durable and payment-safe
steps.title: Orchestrate fulfillment with a managed state machine
steps.content: Use an AWS Step Functions Standard workflow for durable order state, timeouts, retries, compensation, and audit history. An EventBridge Pipe from SQS can start the workflow; use a deterministic execution name and an idempotent start/duplicate policy. This is the only custom node because the current palette has no Step Functions/state-machine component; the generic custom node is explicitly named and keeps its real workflow role visible.

component.label: AWS Step Functions Order Saga
component.description: Durable order/payment workflow with retry and compensation

properties.subtitle: Standard workflow; idempotent order execution
properties.purpose: Orchestrate reserve-confirmed order state, payment authorization/capture, bounded retries, timeout reconciliation, success notification, and compensation that releases reservation on terminal payment failure. Persist workflow execution by stable order ID and never retry an ambiguous charge without checking provider state.
properties.notes: Started through an SQS EventBridge Pipe using a deterministic execution key. External payment remains outside the DynamoDB ACID boundary; use conditional status transitions and idempotent tasks.

component.highlightReason: No existing catalog node represents a durable managed state machine; the supported custom-component is used with an explicit Step Functions identity rather than mislabeling a Lambda or container node.

steps.phase: Make order processing durable and payment-safe
steps.title: Start workflows from SQS without adding synchronous checkout latency
steps.content: An EventBridge Pipe consumes the durable order queue and starts the Standard workflow. Configure retry/DLQ behavior and deterministic execution handling; the pipe is called out in the edge description because no dedicated EventBridge Pipes palette item exists.

connection.label: SQS via EventBridge Pipe
connection.description: Pipe starts an idempotently named Standard workflow; failures retry and redrive without blocking checkout

steps.phase: Make order processing durable and payment-safe
steps.title: Add a narrow payment-provider adapter
steps.content: Keep gateway-specific signing, token exchange, idempotency headers, webhook verification, and response normalization in a small Lambda adapter. Bound connection/read timeouts, rate-limit outbound calls to provider capacity, and distinguish retryable failures from definitive declines.

component.label: Payment Adapter Lambda
component.description: Tokenized, idempotent calls to the payment provider

properties.purpose: Call the gateway with provider token and stable order/payment idempotency key; verify webhook signatures; normalize outcomes; redact logs; reconcile timeouts before retrying a possible charge.
properties.runtime: Small supported runtime with minimal network dependencies
properties.timeout: Bounded below workflow task timeout; explicit connect/read budgets
properties.concurrency: Cap to provider quota and scale only within approved payment-provider throughput
properties.coldStart: Provision warm capacity only if measured payment-start latency requires it; benchmark cold starts against the <1s constraint

component.highlightReason: Serverless Function is the existing Lambda component for a small provider adapter.

steps.title: Invoke payment as a workflow task
steps.content: The workflow passes order ID, amount, currency, and provider token reference—not raw card data—to the adapter. Use a stable payment idempotency key and persist the provider's intent/reference before capture; if the task times out, query provider state before repeating a charge.

connection.label: Tokenized idempotent payment task
connection.description: Workflow invokes adapter with order/payment reference and bounded retry semantics

steps.phase: Make order processing durable and payment-safe
steps.title: Connect to the PCI-compliant payment gateway
steps.content: Use a processor-hosted/tokenized card flow and retain only payment tokens and provider references. The adapter must validate provider certificates, sign/authenticate requests, verify callback signatures and replay timestamps, and exclude sensitive values from logs.

component.label: PCI-Compliant Payment Provider
component.description: Tokenization and external authorization/capture

properties.purpose: Hosted/tokenized card capture, payment intent authorization/capture, signed callbacks, and provider-side idempotency; application stores provider token/reference only and never stores PAN/CVV.
properties.gateway: PCI-compliant external processor; select provider through product/security review
properties.retry: Retry only with stable idempotency key; reconcile ambiguous timeout/provider state before repeating charge

steps.title: Send payment requests only through the adapter
steps.content: Only the payment adapter communicates with the external gateway. The adapter uses TLS, provider credentials from a managed secret, strict egress controls where practical, and an allowlist/contract for the gateway API.

steps.title: Keep provider credentials in managed secrets
steps.content: Store gateway credentials and webhook verification keys in AWS Secrets Manager with KMS-backed encryption, least-privilege read access, rotation where supported, and audit trails. Do not put secrets in Lambda environment plaintext, source control, or traces.

steps.title: Grant only the payment adapter access to its secret
steps.content: The payment Lambda retrieves the specific secret it needs through its execution role. Secret rotation, retrieval failures, and gateway authentication failures are observable without exposing the secret value.

connection.description: Payment adapter role can read only its gateway secret; access is audited

steps.phase: Make order processing durable and payment-safe
steps.title: Persist payment outcomes and compensation state
steps.content: The workflow conditionally updates the order with payment intent/reference and versioned state. On confirmed payment, transition to CONFIRMED; on a definitive terminal failure, release the stock reservation and mark FAILED in a compensating transaction. An ambiguous timeout enters reconciliation rather than an unsafe duplicate charge.

connection.label: Conditional status + compensation
connection.description: Persist payment reference, versioned status, and reservation release/confirmation

steps.phase: Make order processing durable and payment-safe
steps.title: Queue order confirmations after durable success
steps.content: Publish a confirmation event only after the workflow records the successful order transition. A separate notification queue isolates email-provider slowness from checkout and supports controlled retries, deduplication, and DLQ investigation.

component.description: Asynchronous, retryable notification delivery

properties.purpose: Buffer confirmation events emitted after durable CONFIRMED state; deduplicate by order/event ID, retry transient provider errors with backoff, and redrive exhausted messages to an alarmed DLQ.
properties.backoff: Exponential backoff with jitter and bounded DLQ redrive

steps.phase: Make order processing durable and payment-safe
steps.title: Emit a confirmation event only for confirmed orders
steps.content: The workflow writes a notification event with a stable dedupe key after the CONFIRMED transition. Do not send a success email for PENDING_PAYMENT, a decline, or an unverified provider callback.

connection.label: Confirmed order event
connection.description: Only durable successful order transitions enqueue a deduplicated confirmation

steps.phase: Make order processing durable and payment-safe
steps.title: Add an asynchronous notification worker
steps.content: The worker formats a versioned email template from the canonical order record, sends through a managed provider, and records/deduplicates delivery attempts. Keep PII out of logs and never make checkout wait for email delivery.

component.label: Order Notification Lambda
component.description: Idempotent email formatting and delivery worker

properties.purpose: Consume confirmed-order events, load the canonical order, render versioned templates, deduplicate sends by order/event ID, redact PII from logs, and retry transient delivery failures without delaying checkout.
properties.timeout: Bounded provider call with explicit timeout
properties.concurrency: Scale from SQS backlog but cap at email-provider quota

component.highlightReason: Serverless Function is the existing component for a queue-driven notification worker.

steps.phase: Make order processing durable and payment-safe
steps.title: Consume confirmations with bounded retries
steps.content: SQS invokes the notification worker in bounded batches. Use partial batch failure handling so one bad message does not replay successful neighbors; exhausted records go to the DLQ with order/event correlation IDs for safe redrive.

connection.label: SQS-triggered email worker
connection.description: Partial batch retries, idempotent send key, and DLQ for exhausted failures

steps.phase: Make order processing durable and payment-safe
steps.title: Deliver order emails through a managed provider
steps.content: Use Amazon SES or another approved provider for transactional order confirmation. Verify sender identity, configure bounce/complaint handling, avoid marketing consent assumptions, and expose delivery/bounce outcomes separately from the payment/order success state.

component.label: Transactional Email Provider (SES)
component.description: Order confirmation templates and delivery feedback

properties.purpose: Send transactional order confirmation only after durable order success; verify sender, use versioned templates, process bounces/complaints, and keep marketing consent separate.
properties.provider: Amazon SES or approved managed provider
properties.bounceHandling: Process bounce/complaint events and suppress invalid addresses

component.highlightReason: Email Service is an existing component for managed transactional email delivery.

steps.phase: Make order processing durable and payment-safe
steps.title: Send the confirmation without blocking order completion
steps.content: The worker calls the provider asynchronously and records provider message ID/status. A provider outage delays notification but does not roll back a confirmed order or trigger another payment attempt.

connection.label: Transactional confirmation
connection.description: Async delivery with provider message tracking and bounce feedback

steps.phase: Publish inventory changes and prove scale behavior
steps.title: Publish only committed inventory changes
steps.content: A stream consumer turns committed stock/order changes into inventory-change events for interested shoppers. Include SKU, version/sequence, availability state, and a coarse update timestamp; do not expose customer/order data. The update is an asynchronous projection, not the authority used to accept a checkout.

component.label: Inventory Change Publisher Lambda
component.description: DynamoDB Streams projection for committed stock changes

properties.purpose: Consume committed inventory/order stream records, publish minimal SKU availability and monotonic version to the event topic, filter irrelevant changes, and tolerate at-least-once replay without exposing order/customer PII.
properties.concurrency: Tune stream/event-source concurrency to topic and WebSocket fanout capacity

component.highlightReason: Serverless Function is the existing Lambda component for the DynamoDB Streams projection.

steps.phase: Publish inventory changes and prove scale behavior
steps.title: Observe the durable inventory stream
steps.content: Stream delivery is at least once and may be delayed or reordered relative to another partition. Consumers deduplicate and use the inventory version so clients can discard stale updates; checkout still conditionally reserves against DynamoDB's authoritative state.

connection.label: Committed inventory changes
connection.description: DynamoDB Streams feeds the replay-safe inventory projection

steps.phase: Publish inventory changes and prove scale behavior
steps.title: Add an inventory event fan-out topic
steps.content: Use a managed pub/sub topic such as SNS to decouple committed inventory changes from live-client delivery and future consumers. Partition/filter by relevant SKU or tenant where supported, preserve an event version, and avoid broadcasting every stock mutation to every connected user.

component.label: Inventory Update Topic (SNS)
component.description: Filtered fan-out of committed availability changes

properties.purpose: Fan out compact committed SKU availability updates to interested delivery consumers; preserve event version, filter subscriptions by SKU/tenant, and retain no customer/order PII.
properties.fanout: Filtered consumers, not global broadcast to all shoppers
properties.ordering: Consumers compare per-SKU version; do not claim global ordering

component.highlightReason: Pub/Sub is an existing palette component for an SNS-style managed event topic.

steps.phase: Publish inventory changes and prove scale behavior
steps.title: Publish inventory changes after commit
steps.content: The projection publishes a compact versioned message. A retry may publish the same event again, so downstream delivery uses SKU/version deduplication and cannot alter the stock count or order result.

connection.label: Versioned SKU availability event
connection.description: Publish post-commit minimal inventory projection for interested subscribers

steps.phase: Publish inventory changes and prove scale behavior
steps.title: Add the real-time WebSocket API
steps.content: Use API Gateway WebSocket routes for authenticated subscribe/unsubscribe and server-to-client delivery. Authorize connect/subscribe messages, scope subscriptions to a user/tenant, cap message size, and load-test active connection and management-API quotas at 10,000+ sessions.

component.label: Inventory WebSocket API
component.description: Authenticated live inventory subscriptions and pushes

properties.purpose: API Gateway WebSocket connect/subscribe/unsubscribe and management API for live inventory pushes; authenticate connect and subscription routes, enforce tenant/SKU authorization, and benchmark active-session and callback quotas.
properties.inputValidation: Validate route, SKU, tenant, message size, and subscription limits
properties.authentication: JWT/custom authorizer at connect; re-check authorization for subscription changes
properties.rateLimiting: Bound connect, subscribe, and outbound callback rates; shed/coalesce stale updates under pressure

component.highlightReason: A second existing API Gateway component represents the distinct WebSocket protocol endpoint.

steps.phase: Publish inventory changes and prove scale behavior
steps.title: Protect WebSocket handshakes with the edge policy
steps.content: Apply the WAF policy to the WebSocket API stage and reject unauthenticated or abusive connection attempts. The connect authorizer still determines identity; WAF rules only filter traffic patterns.

connection.label: Protected WebSocket handshake
connection.description: WAF filters connection traffic; API authorizer establishes identity

steps.phase: Publish inventory changes and prove scale behavior
steps.title: Persist live connection and subscription ownership
steps.content: Store connection ID, user/tenant, authorized SKU subscriptions, and expiry in DynamoDB with a TTL and access checks. Treat disconnect cleanup as best effort; the broadcaster removes stale IDs after a Gone response. Never use this table as the inventory source of truth.

component.label: WebSocket Connections (DynamoDB)
component.description: Connection ownership, subscriptions, and expiry

properties.purpose: Persist API Gateway connection IDs, verified user/tenant ownership, allowed SKU subscriptions, and TTL; keep separate from authoritative stock records and delete stale connections on Gone callbacks.
properties.workload: Connection/subscription lookups and TTL cleanup for 10,000+ active sessions

component.highlightReason: Database is the existing component for the WebSocket connection registry.

steps.phase: Publish inventory changes and prove scale behavior
steps.title: Register and authorize WebSocket subscriptions
steps.content: The connect/subscribe route writes only the authenticated principal's connection and authorized SKU subscriptions. Use conditional ownership checks and TTL; do not let clients choose another tenant's topics by guessing IDs.

connection.label: Owned connection + SKU subscriptions
connection.description: WebSocket routes persist verified principal, allowed subscriptions, and expiry

steps.phase: Publish inventory changes and prove scale behavior
steps.title: Add a bounded real-time fan-out worker
steps.content: The fan-out worker loads only subscriptions for changed SKUs and batches API Gateway Management API callbacks. Coalesce superseded availability updates during bursts, apply backpressure, retry transient callback failures within a bound, and delete stale connections; reconnecting clients can fetch a fresh authoritative snapshot.

component.label: Inventory WebSocket Fan-out Lambda
component.description: Filtered, bounded push delivery to subscribed clients

properties.purpose: Find authorized subscribers for changed SKU, send compact versioned updates through API Gateway Management API, coalesce superseded events, bound callback concurrency/retries, and remove stale connections; clients resync from authoritative inventory after reconnect.
properties.concurrency: Scale with topic backlog while respecting WebSocket callback quotas

component.highlightReason: Serverless Function is the existing Lambda component for controlled WebSocket fan-out.

steps.phase: Publish inventory changes and prove scale behavior
steps.title: Deliver topic events to the fan-out worker
steps.content: Subscribe the broadcaster to inventory events with SKU/tenant filtering. It compares event versions, ignores stale duplicates, and processes bursts without making the inventory transaction wait for WebSocket delivery.

connection.label: Filtered inventory updates
connection.description: Topic delivers versioned SKU changes to bounded live fan-out

steps.phase: Publish inventory changes and prove scale behavior
steps.title: Resolve subscribers by connection ownership
steps.content: The worker queries the registry by authorized SKU/tenant subscription and applies TTL/ownership checks before sending. If fan-out grows beyond a single partition or batch budget, shard subscription indexes by SKU/tenant and scale consumers while preserving per-SKU version checks.

connection.label: Authorized subscribers by SKU
connection.description: Lookup ownership and subscriptions; stale connection cleanup is idempotent

steps.phase: Publish inventory changes and prove scale behavior
steps.title: Push updates through the WebSocket management API
steps.content: Push only to authorized connections with a monotonically versioned SKU payload. Under overload, coalesce older availability messages and expose the update version so clients can detect gaps and refetch; never let notification delivery decide whether checkout may reserve stock.

connection.label: Versioned live inventory push
connection.description: Management API pushes to authorized active connections; coalesce stale events under load

steps.phase: Publish inventory changes and prove scale behavior
steps.title: Let shoppers subscribe and recover from missed events
steps.content: Clients authenticate a WebSocket session, subscribe only to permitted SKU updates, and compare event versions. On reconnect or a version gap, fetch the current inventory snapshot from the REST API; WebSocket events are a low-latency projection, not a durable client-side ledger.

connection.label: Authenticated live stock updates
connection.description: Clients reconnect and resync authoritative availability after a missed version

steps.phase: Publish inventory changes and prove scale behavior
steps.title: Measure correctness, latency, and spend together
steps.content: Track API p95/p99 and throttles, Lambda cold starts/concurrency/errors, DynamoDB throttles/transaction conflicts/hot keys, SQS oldest-message age and DLQ count, workflow/payment outcomes, email delivery, WebSocket active connections/callback failures, and inventory event freshness. Alert on business correctness signals as well as infrastructure health.

component.label: Commerce Reliability + Cost Monitoring
component.description: End-to-end order correctness, scale, and latency signals

properties.purpose: Correlate request/order IDs across API, functions, DynamoDB, SQS, workflow, gateway, notifications, and WebSockets; alert on cold-start latency, throttles, transaction conflicts, queue age/DLQ, payment ambiguity, inventory freshness, callback failures, and cost per order.
properties.metrics: API p95/p99; Lambda init/concurrency/errors; DynamoDB throttles/conflicts; queue age/DLQ; workflow/payment outcomes; email bounces; active sockets and inventory update lag
properties.alerts: Page on correctness/data-loss indicators and SLO burn; ticket on cost/headroom trends
properties.retention: Set by security, audit, and cost policy; redact sensitive fields

component.highlightReason: Monitoring is an existing palette component for service health and business-level reliability signals.

steps.phase: Publish inventory changes and prove scale behavior
steps.title: Observe API and Lambda saturation
steps.content: Publish request latency, throttles, authorization failures, cold starts, concurrency saturation, and errors to the monitoring path with correlation IDs. Keep payloads and card/payment credentials out of telemetry.

connection.label: API latency + throttles
connection.description: Route-level p95/p99, WAF/API throttles, and trace correlation

steps.phase: Publish inventory changes and prove scale behavior
steps.title: Observe storage and queue pressure
steps.content: Monitor DynamoDB transaction conflicts, throttled requests, consumed capacity, and hot partition keys alongside oldest SQS message age, retries, and DLQ depth. Scale or shed work based on the constrained downstream service, not just Lambda invocation count.

connection.label: Transactions + capacity signals
connection.description: Monitor reservation conflicts, throttles, hot keys, queue lag, and cost

steps.phase: Publish inventory changes and prove scale behavior
steps.title: Validate the design before calling the constraints met
steps.content: Run a sale-shaped load test with 10,000+ active users, measured burst and sustained request rates, skewed hot SKUs, duplicate checkout retries, delayed/duplicate stream events, queue and provider outages, cold Lambda starts, WebSocket reconnects, and ambiguous payment timeouts. Verify no oversell or duplicate charge, every committed order is recoverable from its outbox, terminal payment failure releases stock, and notifications remain asynchronous. Report cold-start latency against the strict <1s constraint, API/order latency and live-update freshness against explicitly agreed targets, concurrency/quota headroom, queue drain time, failure recovery, and cost per successful order. The brief does not provide the numeric traffic curve, live-update SLO, availability target, or budget, so do not claim those unknowns are satisfied until stakeholders set and tests validate them.
